policies.description: A configuration item may be linked to an incident only when its **status** is **in_use** or **maintenance**; it must **not** be linked when the status is **retired** or **disposed**.
references: • CI Status: Only CIs with status = in_use or status = maintenance can be linked to active Incidents. Do not link CIs in status = retired or status = disposed.

policies.description: Only users with the **Agent** or **Manager** role have permission to create, read, update, or delete CMDB records, which includes linking a CI to an incident.
references: | Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings. |

policies.description: Both **configuration_item** and **incident_id** are required parameters for the link operation and must be supplied before the call is made.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Before invoking the **link_affected_ci_to_incident** tool, the assistant must verify that both the incident and the configuration item exist. Use the provided lookup tools (**find_incident_by_id**, **find_incident_by_number**, **find_configuration_item_by_serial_number**, **find_configuration_items**) to retrieve the records. Proceed with the link only if the look‑up calls succeed and return valid IDs. Never fabricate or guess any ID; always rely on the concrete API responses.
references: When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.description: When invoking the **link_affected_ci_to_incident** tool, the call must be the only operational API request in the current transaction (i.e., exactly one validated operation). Do not combine this call with any other create/update/delete actions unless you are using an explicitly approved batch endpoint that supports atomic multi‑record processing.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.
